Source text (read all of it):
<<<
Passaging Two Flasks of Adherent HEK293 Cells

Two T75 flasks at about 90 % confluence are split 1:6 into four new flasks. The room has one biosafety cabinet, one 37 °C water bath, one CO₂ incubator, one benchtop centrifuge and one microscope with a haemocytometer. Only one flask can be open in the cabinet at a time, so the two flasks queue for it while the centrifuge and the microscope stay free. Work with pre-warmed medium, PBS and trypsin-EDTA throughout; nothing cold touches the cells. One operator.

Preparation
1. Wipe down the cabinet, lay out pipettes and tubes, and let the blower run; 10 minutes.
2. Check both flasks on the microscope for confluence and contamination; 10 minutes.

Flask A
3. Aspirate the spent medium and rinse the monolayer with 5 mL of PBS; 4 minutes in the cabinet.
4. Add 2 mL of trypsin-EDTA, rock the flask and return it to the incubator for 5 minutes.
5. Knock the flask, check detachment and neutralise with 8 mL of medium; 5 minutes in the cabinet.
6. Transfer the suspension to a 15 mL tube and spin at 300 × g for 5 minutes.
7. Aspirate the supernatant and resuspend the pellet in 10 mL of fresh medium; 4 minutes.
8. Count the cells on the haemocytometer; 6 minutes.
9. Seed two new T75 flasks at 1:6 and label them; 6 minutes in the cabinet.
10. Return the new flasks to the incubator and leave them to settle overnight, at least 16 hours.

Flask B
11. Start flask B the moment flask A leaves the cabinet: aspirate and rinse with 5 mL of PBS; 4 minutes.
12. Trypsinise flask B in the incubator for 5 minutes.
13. Neutralise flask B as soon as flask A is out of the cabinet again; 5 minutes.
14. Spin flask B at 300 × g for 5 minutes once the centrifuge is free.
15. Resuspend the flask B pellet in 10 mL of fresh medium; 4 minutes.
16. Count flask B on the haemocytometer once flask A has been counted; 6 minutes.
17. Seed two more T75 flasks at 1:6 and label them; 6 minutes.
18. Return them to the incubator to settle overnight alongside the first pair.

Finishing
19. Wipe the cabinet down, discard the waste and switch the blower to standby; 10 minutes.
20. Write the passage number, the split ratio and the counts into the culture log; 5 minutes.
>>>

One operator is doing everything, and the single biosafety cabinet is the critical shared resource because only one flask can be open in it at a time; Flask B is timed to begin its rinse when Flask A leaves the cabinet, and later cabinet work is gated by Flask A being out again. The room has only one 37 °C water bath, one CO₂ incubator, one benchtop centrifuge, one microscope/haemocytometer setup, and one operator, so incubation, spinning, counting, and seeding must be sequenced without conflicting for those resources. A track is one sequential line of work, so steps in the same track never overlap, while anything that happens at the same time as something else belongs in a different track. A step has exactly one duration kind: `fixed` with `seconds`, `variable` with `minSeconds`, `maxSeconds`, and `defaultSeconds`, or `indefinite` until the person ends it. A `startTrigger` attaches a step to the clock or another step using `programStart`, `programStartOffset`, `afterStep`, `afterStepWithBuffer`, `manual`, `onAbort`, or `compound`. `stepId`s are unique across the whole program, not just within one track, so every referenced `stepId` must resolve globally. Every `task` occupied by a step needs a matching `resourceConstraints` entry, and `maxConcurrent` is what prevents two steps from sharing one cabinet, microscope, centrifuge, incubator slot, or operator. Repeated `n`-item work should be modeled as `replicates` on one step rather than copied steps, using `instances: "each"` for per-instance chains, `instances: "all"` for barriers, and `maxInFlight` when a holding area limits how many repetitions can be in flight at once.

- `microscope`: 1 — only one microscope/haemocytometer station.  
- `co2_incubator`: 4 — one incubator, but it must be able to hold up to four seeded flasks at once; it also needs to permit two source flasks trypsinizing concurrently if that is modeled.  
- `centrifuge`: 1 — only one benchtop centrifuge.  
- `water_bath`: 1 — one 37 °C water bath, included as a constraint even if the source text does not give an explicit timed water-bath step.  
- `operator`: 1 — one operator performs all hands-on work, unless the runner’s `actors` setting is used instead; I still expect one operator.

Take the step list from turn 3 exactly as it stands.

**First, tracks.** Put each step in a track: one track per parallel line of work — per dish, per station, per instrument, per performer, per sample group. Steps in one track run one after another and must not overlap; anything that runs while something else runs belongs in its own track.

**Second, triggers.** Give every step a `startTrigger` from this vocabulary and no other:

- `{"type":"programStart"}` — at t = 0.
- `{"type":"programStartOffset","offsetSeconds":n}` — n seconds after the start; this is how a short track is delayed so it finishes with the others.
- `{"type":"afterStep","stepId":"x"}` — when x ends. Add `"offsetSeconds"` for a gap, `"event":"start"` to hang off x's start instead of its end, `"instances"` when x is replicated.
- `{"type":"afterStepWithBuffer","stepId":"x","bufferSeconds":n}` — n seconds after x ends.
- `{"type":"manual"}` — the person taps to start it: a gate that no clock can predict (guests seated, dough looks right, the surgeon is ready).
- `{"type":"compound","logic":"all"|"any","triggers":[...]}` — wait for all of, or the first of, several triggers.

**Third, refine the question before you answer it.** Within the scope of scheduling these activities for one person to follow, suggest a better version of the question "which activities depend on which, and which can run at the same time?" — one that would expose dependencies this text implies but does not state: things that must cool, rest, preheat, thaw, proof, be held warm, or be ready at the same moment as something else. Write your improved question out, answer it, and revise the triggers accordingly. A step the improved question reveals is added here, marked `"inferred": true`.

1. If the public catalog already covers this (search_public_recipes or run_protocol), load that instead and stop — its result already has the live URL.
2. Otherwise keep the program you just built; `rhylthyme://guide/authoring` is the cheat-sheet and `rhylthyme://examples/*` are complete programs to pattern-match.
3. Express the limits as constraints, not as copied JSON: the `resourceConstraints`, `replicates`, `instances` and `maxInFlight` you confirmed in turn 2.
4. Run validate_program and fix every error it reports.
5. Run analyze_schedule to check the makespan, critical path and resource conflicts; adjust offsets so tracks finish together. Its `bindingConstraints` say which limit is actually gating the makespan.
6. Call visualize_schedule and give the user the live URL plus the Gantt/itinerary from the result. Do not describe the schedule in prose.
